newsitem.title: FRANCE: Op Art painter Vasarely dies at 88 in Paris. [CORRECTED 11:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Op Art painter Vasarely dies at 88 in Paris. [CORRECTED 11:30 GMT]

text.p: Hungarian-born French painter Victor Vasarely, one of the stars of the Op Art movement in the 1960s whose geometrical works played on optical illusion, died in Paris on Saturday night, his daughter-in-law said on Sunday.
Vasarely, born in Pecs on April 9, 1908 (corrects from 1906), died at a Paris hospital where he had been treated for cancer for the last two years, Michele Vasarely said.
He moved to Paris in 1930 and achieved world fame more than 30 years later when his colourful abstract works, creating the illusion of movement, became widely popular.

In 1971, he created a foundation bearing his name in the southern French city of Aix-en-Provence which drew hundreds of thousands of visitors to a museum of his "kinetic art", opened five years later.

But the foundation, bailed out to the tune of 18.9 million francs ($3 million) by public authorities in 1993 amid legal disputes over its management, was placed in court-supervised liquidation last month.

A report by tax authorities said hundreds of works with a total value of 42 million francs ($8.4 million) had disappeared between 1982 and 1993, when the foundation was administered by Aix-Marseille university.
The former president of the foundation, law professor Charles Debbasch, has been placed under judicial investigation in the case.
